clinical_knowledge.topic: Rotator cuff tendinopathy evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Rotator cuff tendinopathy is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy: Physical therapy (rotator cuff strengthening), NSAIDs, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: aching shoulder pain when reaching overhead

Key HPI features: A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic with aching shoulder pain when reaching overhead. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Rotator cuff tendinopathy.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Rotator cuff tear without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Progressive weakness would suggest tear rather than tendinopathy.
management_principles: Plan for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy: Physical therapy (rotator cuff strengthening), NSAIDs
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.
